text:
alex: FYI nodes in ap-southeast1 are hitting repeated nvme metadata errors after the midnight scrub window. GPU pods going readonly and evicting.

maria: saw panicked alerts. how many nodes?

alex: ~7 gnodes showed blk_update_request: I/O error and then the kernel remounted overlay as read-only. GPU scheduler then evicted pods due to attach failures.

jon: any recent kernel/drivers changed?

alex: no kernel bump. We did increase janitor scrub aggressiveness (scrub --deep) last deploy to catch stale tombstones. Likely correlation.

sophia: logs from one node:
```
[2026-03-21T00:12:03Z] nvme0: health critical: metadata mismatch
[2026-03-21T00:12:03Z] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 987654
[2026-03-21T00:12:04Z] overlayfs: lowerdir: remounting read-only
```

maria: that's nasty. Are we seeing SMART errors or just transient io errors?

alex: SMART shows rising media_errors on those drives. Not all nodes in pool; pattern matches devices provisioned in a 2-week window (same SKU batch).

jon: could be a firmware regression or manufacturer batch issue. Need to isolate and avoid scheduling GPUs there.

sophia: immediate mitigation: cordon nodes and drain GPU pods, mark them as io-isolated in fleet. Also disable deep scrub until we validate.

maria: agree. Also create a temp admission rule for scheduler to prefer healthy-nvme taint.

alex: started cordon+drain on 7 nodes (ap-southeast1-c) now. Moving running workloads to spare capacity in us-west2 for memory-heavy jobs.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0462  NVMe metadata errors causing read-only remounts  severity P1.

jon: ops: can you query provisioning history and map the affected instances to vendor batch? If yes, open a vendor RMA / investigation.

sophia: querying... Yep, all 7 map to SKU XNV-9800 firmware 1.2.3 and proc batch B-47. Opening vendor ticket RTV-2026-21.

maria: policy/cost question: we just had 12% capacity loss in the zone. Routing those jobs cross-region will add egress and possible preemption. Ops, what's our temporary capacity buffer?

sophia: we have ~18% spare in nearby zones but not guaranteed. Cross-region fallback will cost ~3.2% extra on those runs (egress + preempt).

alex: can we hot-swap nodes with cold spares in the same region but different SKU? Prefer that over cross-region shift if available.

sophia: 4 compatible hot-spares available, will allocate them. Still need to replace the defective SKUs.

jon: medium term: add an nvme health classifier that tags nodes based on SMART metrics + error rates and prevents GPU scheduling past a soft threshold. Also avoid running deep scrub on nodes where media_errors > 0.

maria: +1. Also we should add an alert when overlay remounts read-only more than twice in 10m. That's a clear signal.

alex: added a short-run runbook notes to the incident: 1) cordon/drain affected nodes, 2) disable deep-scrub, 3) allocate hot-spares, 4) open vendor RMA, 5) schedule node retirement and rebuild from fresh NVMe.

sophia: filing the vendor RMA now and tagging hw-team. ETA from vendor is 5 business days.

maria: cost note for leadership: anticipated one-week degraded capacity in ap-southeast1 - recommend temporary reserved burst from Dedicated pool to cover customer SLOs if needed. Estimate additional monthly cost ~2.0x for that burst on the reserved fraction.

jon: quick workaround: set a per-node kernel param to limit scrub read concurrency (vm.dirty_bytes or scrub concurrency tunable) to reduce IO pressure while we rotate drives. Not ideal if hardware is bad, but may buy time.

alex: patched affected nodes to set scrub concurrency to 1 and reduced overlayfs writeback timeouts. seeing fewer remounts but SMART still shows media_errors.

ops-bot: update INC-2026-0462: 7 nodes cordoned, 4 hot-spares allocated, vendor RMA opened.

sophia: will start controlled repro on one retired node to capture full nvme SMART dump for vendor.

maria: great. after we replace drives, we should run a soak test for 48h under P99 load before returning to normal scrub aggressiveness. Also update fleet policy to avoid aggressive scrubs on same batch SKUs.

alex: agreed. Adding follow-up tasks to infra backlog and linking to incident. Closing thread here, will update incident with RMA progress. :wave:
